src.label: Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Embassy in the USA) — pet animals: rules for entering Greece

head: Pets from outside the EU must enter through an authorised border inspection post, with a microchip and rabies vaccine.
lines: The Greek foreign ministry page says dogs, cats and ferrets coming from a third country may enter only through an authorised border inspection post. It lists Athens International Airport, Thessaloniki airport and port and Piraeus port, plus a set of island ports and airports such as Rhodes, Kos, Chios, Heraklion, Chania and Corfu.

Over three months of age, the animal needs an ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or a readable tattoo), a rabies vaccine, and an official veterinarian's certificate. A rabies antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml, taken 30 days or more after vaccination, is required when the animal comes from a country outside the listed low-risk group.

The page also says pets travelling by public transport must be in a safe cage labelled with the owner's name, address and phone number. The text refers to older EU decisions, so confirm current wording with the Greek veterinary authority.
